description: We are students and technology professionals with backgrounds in web development, data analysis, technical support, and applied AI. We are drawn to this challenge because it combines real data with a product designed for users working under demanding conditions. We are looking for team members with experience in data visualization, programming (Python or JavaScript), geospatial data, or UX design, and with a willingness to iterate and communicate ideas clearly.
summary:
AresRoute is an interactive web platform designed to make it easier to explore and plan routes across the surface of Mars, using scientific data from NASA and the USGS.

The platform features a 3D Martian globe, interactive maps of craters such as Jezero and Gale, and an intelligent route-planning system. Using A* search algorithms and real digital elevation models, AresRoute analyzes slopes, proposes alternative paths, and lets users compare distances, estimated travel times, and terrain risks through clear visual indicators.

We are also integrating ARES, an AI copilot that lets users query scientific information and interact with the platform through voice commands.

AresRoute turns complex scientific information into a visual, accessible, and intuitive tool that helps people understand the challenges of mobility and human exploration on Mars. It aims to bring Mars mission planning closer to students, researchers, and future explorers, supporting data-driven decisions while acknowledging the limits of simulations and the available terrain data.
details:
AresRoute - Navigate Mars. Explore the Future.

Project Overview
AresRoute is an interactive Mars exploration platform designed to make planetary exploration more accessible, educational, and engaging. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our project addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by combining real planetary data, interactive mapping, 3D visualization, and artificial intelligence.

How Does It Work?
Users can explore Mars through an interactive 3D globe, navigate detailed orbital maps of Jezero Crater, and visualize Martian terrain. The platform integrates NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera (CTX), Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), Mars Odyssey THEMIS imagery, and historical Viking mapping data. Users can select locations, create exploration plans, compare alternative routes, and examine terrain-related information. The application also includes an AI-powered assistant to support interactive exploration and help users understand the Martian environment.

Technologies Used
We developed AresRoute using React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, and OpenLayers. Our solution incorporates NASA Mars Trek planetary mapping services, USGS terrain datasets, and cloud-based AI technologies using Amazon Web Services and Amazon Bedrock. The web application is deployed through Vercel, allowing users to access it directly from their browsers.

Innovation and Creativity
AresRoute transforms complex scientific information into an interactive experience that combines planetary mapping, 3D visualization, exploratory route planning, and conversational AI. Rather than presenting NASA datasets as isolated scientific resources, our platform connects them through a unified interface designed for accessibility and exploration.

Challenges and Considerations
Our team considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, geographic coverage, usability, performance, and accessibility. We clearly distinguish observed planetary data from simulations and estimates. Route calculations are exploratory and educational; they are not validated for actual astronaut navigation or mission safety.

Future Impact
Our vision is to evolve AresRoute into a platform that supports planetary education, scientific outreach, and future research into human exploration of Mars. By making NASA’s open data more accessible, we hope to inspire students, developers, researchers, and future explorers to engage with planetary science.
